name: apollo11
title: Apollo 11, read whole
claim: An agent that is never shown an image reads NASA's Apollo 11 archive through its eyes, writes the landing minute by minute with every sentence citing a look, survives a kill inside the evidence sink, and pays for each look once.

oneOf.why: The lead (openai/gpt-6-luna), and the eyes too when it is the only key (openai/gpt-6-sol).
The eyes (google/gemini-3.8-flash), and the lead too when it is the only key.
The lead and the eyes (anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5) when it is the only key.
An OpenAI-compatible gateway that serves the models under their public ids, instead of provider keys.
oneOf.where: your gateway's base URL, ending in /v1

keys.why: A model provider's key for --live (the run names every model by provider and public id).

programs.why: Cuts the film's windows into frames for the eyes (with ffprobe).
Reads the film's length and size.
Renders the scanned pages; without it PDFium, which installs with the repository, renders them.

kills.why: Inside the evidence sink: the eyes have answered forty looks and the answers are kept, and the looks reaching the sink now are not yet filed. A fresh process reads those answers back: kept, not paid again.

input.shape: examples/apollo11/workflow.ts, INPUT: the film's window range, the scan's page range, the photos by id, the account's span of mission time

variants.examples/apollo11/inputs/gallery.json: the gallery take: 8 film windows, 10 pages (the 1202 alarm to the landing), 12 photos
variants.examples/apollo11/inputs/full.json: the whole archive: all 626 pages, the film's descent in 26 windows, all 60 photos (about $3.50)
variants.examples/apollo11/inputs/weak-eyes.json: the weak-eyes pass: the landing's 40 pages and the 60 photos, no film; run it with --eyes-model openai/gpt-6-luna
